content: Swish the liquid extract orally and swallow three times daily. Use 10 to 15 drops of the liquid extract diluted in 100 mL of warm water. Administer 1 mL orally three times daily (Iberogast, Medical Futures, Inc). Alternatively, take 2 to 8 grams orally three times daily. Another option is to consume 1 cup orally three to four times daily. For dried flower heads, use 3 grams steeped in 150 mL of water. Administer 1 to 4 mL orally three times daily, prepared as a 1:1 solution in 45% alcohol. For topical application, use a 3% to 10% ointment or gel as needed. This treatment is indicated for conditions such as flatulence, gastrointestinal inflammatory disorders, gastrointestinal spasms, skin or mucous membrane inflammation, insomnia, menstrual cramps, and motion sickness. Topical applications are specifically used for hemorrhoids and chemotherapy-induced mucositis. The German Commission E classifies this treatment as effective. It is possibly effective for dyspepsia, colic, and mucositis. This treatment is generally regarded as safe. However, potential adverse reactions include anaphylaxis, contact dermatitis, hypersensitivity reactions, and vomiting. Individuals with hypersensitivity to plants in the Asteraceae/Compositae family (e.g., chrysanthemums, daisies, marigolds, ragweed) should avoid use. Caution is advised in patients with asthma or those taking concurrent CYP3A4 substrates. During pregnancy, this treatment is categorized as avoid use. For lactation, there is no available data. However, in general, it is considered acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
